invariants.rule: The high-capability Agent owns project-level understanding and key decisions.
Executors perform bounded work and cannot redefine project intent or become the canonical project planner.
Every executable capability must expose the common Component/Block boundary with declared inputs and outputs.
The kernel must not require a fixed Product-Design-Build-QA-Delivery sequence.
The Agent expands a CapabilityTree and executable dependencies compile to one ExecutionDAG.
Project-team roles are capability bundles or views and never mandatory kernel stages.
A failure invalidates and reruns the smallest safely identifiable affected subgraph.
New reusable capabilities enter through a validated interface and tests before registry reuse.
Self-growth may add or replace capabilities but cannot silently weaken product invariants or create a second kernel authority.
High-cost Agent calls are reserved for decisions deterministic logic or bounded cheap executors cannot safely make.
